item.title: A Houston lawyer bought a 15,000-sq-ft mansion listed for $15.5 million just to demolish it
item.description: In River Oaks, Houston lawyer Tony Buzbee has bought a mansion primarily for property expansion. Teaming up with Habitat for Humanity, he aims to salvage valuable construction materials, which will provide substantial support—millions of pounds worth—for affordable housing projects. The planned demolition will allow for the development of a larger private garden estate while enhancing his family's legacy through philanthropic efforts.

item.title: In 2024, a Colorado county paid $34 million for a 650-acre ranch owned for more than a century
item.description: In a momentous conservation victory, a historic ranch in Colorado has been designated as protected wilderness. This expansion secures an impressive 530 acres of public land, which local officials successfully purchased through a record-breaking deal two years prior. After being privately held for more than a century, this acquisition ensures the enduring protection of crucial wildlife habitats and public access to the land.

item.title: Texas farmer loses 600 acres to Google data centre, given just 60 days to leave
item.description: In rural Texas, expansive tracts of farmland are increasingly being repurposed for technology ventures, primarily data centers by major tech enterprises. This shift is impacting farmers, especially with resource competition over vital necessities like water. Concerns have been raised by state officials regarding the permanent loss of fertile land, highlighting a significant transition in the region's agricultural landscape.

item.title: Japan killed 14,000+ bears after record attacks; 6 people died despite cull, 8,800 more targeted
item.description: Japan is currently grappling with a significant rise in bear conflicts, with incidents surging alarmingly. Conservationists are voicing urgent concerns regarding the extensive culling of endangered bear populations. Factors such as extreme heat and declining food sources are pushing bears into human territories in search of food. While the government’s response aims at curtailing bear numbers, critics label this approach as ineffective.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1856, one of Northern California’s oldest cattle ranches was established; 170 years later...
item.description: In a landmark initiative, the Wildlands Conservancy is set to acquire the AP Ranch in Northern California, establishing an impressive public preserve in Siskiyou County. This strategic 14,177-acre purchase will unite with an existing land reserve, exceeding 20,000 acres in total. The project aims to protect essential wildlife corridors and headwaters within the Scott River watershed, while also facilitating habitat restoration and free recreational access for visitors.

item.title: Relocated turtle nests produced fewer hatchlings, smaller young and a heavily female-biased sex ratio
item.description: Relocating vulnerable sea turtle nests can lead to unexpected negative consequences. When nests are moved to warmer areas, the sex ratio of hatchlings skews heavily towards females. Additionally, even nests placed in shaded locations yield smaller hatchlings with reduced physical capabilities. Therefore, effective nest relocation must consider various environmental factors beyond just temperature to ensure the successful recovery of turtle populations.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: German tourist returns stolen skull to Vienna cathedral after 60 years with a final confession
item.description: A human skull that was stolen from the catacombs of St. Stephen's Cathedral in Vienna has been returned to its rightful place. The elderly German tourist who had taken it as a young man confessed after sixty long years, seeking closure for his past actions. Although the identity of the original owner is a mystery, this return marks the resolution of a tale filled with youthful folly and subsequent regret.

item.title: Meet Reyha Raghavaraju, the 16-year-old baker bringing birthday joy to families in need
item.description: Reyha Raghavaraju launched Birthday Bundles after witnessing a child's uncelebrated birthday. This compassionate program offers homemade cakes and gifts to families in need. Now, with the enthusiastic involvement of volunteers, they curate unique birthday bundles, reaching more than 136 families in metro Atlanta. Birthday Bundles strives to make every child feel cherished and celebrated, regardless of their circumstances.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Nepal floods: How recent reports warned of this disaster months ago
item.description: Recent floods in Nepal and Tibet followed ICIMOD's warnings about melting glaciers. These reports highlighted doubled ice loss rates and increased flood risks across the region. A catastrophic flash flood triggered by a glacier collapse killed hundreds and left many missing. Smaller glaciers are shrinking faster, intensifying hazards like glacial lake outburst floods. Regional cooperation is vital for understanding and preparing for these cross-border mountain disasters.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: A 16-year-old Irish student turned lost hurling balls in the dark into a €40,000 glow-ball business
item.description: Cathal Sweeney has revolutionized winter hurling training with the creation of his glow-in-the-dark Glo Ball. Utilizing unique phosphorescent materials, this innovative product enhances visibility during low light conditions. Launched under the student enterprise GLO Hurling, the Glo Ball soared in sales and earned top honors in the Senior Category at the 2026 Student Enterprise Programme Finals, exemplifying how creativity can turn challenges into opportunities.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Scientists turn wood waste into foam that replaces plastic and decomposes in soil within months
item.description: Canada is piloting a new process to convert wood waste into biodegradable foam. This innovative material is designed to replace plastic foam packaging and construction insulation. The pilot plant in Vancouver currently produces a limited amount of this eco-friendly wood foam. Future plans include expanding production significantly within Indigenous territories and on Vancouver Island. This initiative aims to create jobs and foster economic opportunities for Indigenous communities.
